title: Votic for English speakers
description: A beginner course in Votic, on of the critically endangered uralic languages of Russia. Learn greetings, introduce yourself, get around.

units.title: Greetings & first words
units.topic: Difficulty 1 · Start with useful greetings and polite expressions.
units.notes:
## Votic basics

Votic uses the Latin alphabet with additional **accents**. ##Vocabulary 

| Votic | English |
| --- | --- |
| tere | hi |
| miä õõn | I am |
| siä õõd | you are | 
 | -ko | questions marker | 
 | üvva omnikkoa | good morning | 
 | üvva päivää | good afternoon | 
 | üvva ohtõgoa | good night | 


 ##Verb conjugation 
As you can see from the words for 'I am', and 'you are', we use the stem 'õõ' to mean 'to be'. The infinitive (simplest form) of the verb is actually 'õlla', however verb stems often differ greatly from their infinitive in Votic. units.title: Food & cafés
units.topic: Difficulty 2 · Learn common food and drink words, then make a polite order.
units.notes:
## At a café

- `nước` — water
- `cà phê` — coffee
- `cơm` — rice / a meal
- `làm ơn` — please

A simple polite request is **Cho tôi ___, làm ơn** (Please give me ___).

units.title: Getting around
units.topic: Difficulty 3 · Ask simple questions and understand useful travel phrases.
units.notes:
## Handy travel phrases

- `ở đâu?` — where is it?
- `ở đây` — here
- `ở kia` — over there
- `Tôi muốn đi…` — I want to go…

Vietnamese does not conjugate verbs for each person: `tôi đi` means “I go,” and `bạn đi` means “you go.”
